predictions.prediction_text: US equities are expected to face increased volatility and downside risk if Trump continues to fail to bring certainty to the economy and markets.
predictions.expected_result: Increased intraday and larger-than-normal weekly drawdowns in broad US equity indices (e.g., S&P 500 declines >3% within a week) following further political uncertainty from Trump.

predictions.prediction_text: US tech stocks will disproportionately benefit from AI themes and be preferred for long-term (yearly) outperformance.
predictions.expected_result: Relative outperformance of tech-heavy indices (e.g., QQQ vs. S&P 500) over a 12-month horizon, with QQQ total return exceeding S&P 500 total return.

predictions.prediction_text: Short-term yields will remain pressured downward after the Fed's hawkish cut flattened the curve and tempered December expectations, keeping front-end yields lower.
predictions.expected_result: 1-3 month Treasury yields stay below pre-cut levels or decline further over the next month.

predictions.prediction_text: Quality bonds should be favored as hedges despite short-term yield pops.
predictions.expected_result: Outperformance of high-quality fixed income (e.g., investment-grade government or corporate bond ETFs) versus equities during episodes of market stress over the next quarter.

predictions.prediction_text: Equities have not priced in the risk of large tariff refunds if Trump loses the IEEPA case, implying downside risk once the market recognizes potential fiscal impact.
predictions.condition: SCOTUS rules that Trump unlawfully used IEEPA to impose tariffs
predictions.expected_result: Repricing that leads to a drop in affected sectors (import-exposed companies) and overall market decline, e.g., sector indexes down >5% within days of the ruling.

predictions.prediction_text: Ad-hoc bilateral trade deals inject uncertainty and may cause market volatility despite temporary positive headlines.
predictions.expected_result: Spikes in realized volatility measures (e.g., VIX increases >20% from baseline) following announcements of ad-hoc trade deals or reversals.
